questions.stem: `SessionKey` was a hand-written class whose IDE-generated `equals` and `hashCode` covered `userId` and `device`. The team replaced it with `record SessionKey(String userId, String device)` and, a month later, added a third component, `String tenant`. A `HashMap` holds a session under (`u-81`, `tablet`, `north`). What does a lookup with a new key (`u-81`, `tablet`, `south`) return?

options.text: The north tenant's session, since the tenant was added after the record's equals had been generated
options.says: a record's equals and hashCode are derived from the component list in the header, so the tenant is part of them as soon as it is declared

options.text: The north tenant's session, since a record's hashCode reads only the components its first version declared
options.says: the generated hashCode reads every component in the current header

options.text: null, since the record's equals and hashCode cover the tenant once it is in the header
options.says: a record derives equals and hashCode from its component list, so the two keys differ, as the record key missed for AT

options.text: null, since the record's equals compares the stored key and the new key by reference
options.says: a record compares component values; two separately built keys with equal values are equal, as the record DE request shows

origin.section: A Record's equals and hashCode Follow Its Component List, So a New Field Can't Be Left Out

questions.stem: `record Reading(String sensor, double value)` gains a third component, `Instant at`. The code base uses it in three places: `new Reading(id, v)` in a parser, `case Reading(var s, var v) ->` in a switch, and `r.value()` in a report. Which of the three stop compiling?

options.text: The constructor call and the switch case, since both must list every component of the header
options.says: the canonical constructor and the record pattern both take the full header; javac reports a wrong argument count and 'incorrect number of nested patterns', while an accessor call is unaffected

options.text: The constructor call and the accessor call, since both name members the old header declared
options.says: value() is still an accessor of the new record, so r.value() compiles; the pattern is what breaks

options.text: The switch case and the accessor call, since both read components out of an existing reading
options.says: the accessor value() still exists, so r.value() compiles; the constructor call is what breaks besides the pattern

options.text: All three, since each one was compiled against the header the record had before
options.says: code that reads only some components, such as r.value(), is not affected by a new component

origin.section: Adding a Component Breaks Every Constructor Call and Record Pattern at Compile Time

questions.stem: `record Batch(String id, Set<String> skus)` has no compact constructor. A `HashSet<Batch> shipped` holds a batch built from the caller's own `HashSet` of SKUs. Later the caller adds a SKU to that set of SKUs, then asks `shipped.contains(batch)` with the very same `batch` object. What does it return?

options.text: true, since the record's final field still points at the same Set object as before
options.says: the field is final, but the set it refers to changed, and the record's hashCode reads its contents

options.text: true, since a record works out its hash code once, when it is constructed
options.says: the record's hash follows its components: in the Leg run the hash changed after the list changed, and get() missed

options.text: false, since the batch's hash code changed along with its set of SKUs
options.says: the record is only shallowly immutable: the SKU set changed, so the hash changed and the lookup searches the wrong bucket

options.text: false, since equals now compares the batch's changed SKU set with an older copy of it
options.says: the record holds the caller's set itself, not a copy; the stored batch is this very object and still equals it ('key equals: true' in the Leg run), but the lookup searches the bucket of the new hash

origin.section: A Record Is Only Shallowly Immutable: a List Component Can Change Under a Map Key

questions.stem: A retry queue keeps `RetryRequest` DTOs in a `LinkedHashSet`. Two clients each send a retry for order `o-5520`, attempt 3, and each arrives as its own object. The DTO used to be a JavaBean; it is now `record RetryRequest(String orderId, int attempt)`. How many entries does the set hold after both arrive?

options.text: Two, since each request with that order id and attempt is still its own object
options.says: a record's equals compares component values, so two separate objects with equal values are one set element

options.text: Two, since the record compares the order id and attempt by reference, as the bean compared requests
options.says: a record compares its components' values, not the references of the requests or their parts; the bean was the one comparing references

options.text: One, since the record compares the order id and attempt values of the two requests
options.says: the bean compared identity and was counted twice; the record compares values, so the second retry is a duplicate

options.text: One, since the record's hash of order id and attempt puts both in a bucket where the set keeps the first
options.says: equal hash codes only bring the two requests together; the record's equals is what makes the second a duplicate

origin.section: Moving a JavaBean DTO to a Record Turns Identity into Value Equality
